zh: （工作上的）餘力、可分配的時間精力
definition: the time and energy someone has available to deal with something
example: I don't have the bandwidth to take on another project this month.
example_zh: 我這個月沒有餘力再接另一個專案。

definition: to change the time of something so that it happens later
example: Can we push back the meeting to Thursday?
example_zh: 我們可以把會議延到星期四嗎？

zh: 排定優先順序、優先處理
definition: to decide which things are most important and deal with them first
example: We need to prioritize the client's bug fixes over new features.
example_zh: 我們要先處理客戶回報的錯誤，新功能往後放。

definition: a balance between two things, where getting more of one means getting less of the other
example: There's always a trade-off between speed and quality.
example_zh: 速度和品質之間總是要有所取捨。

definition: possible to do and likely to work
example: Is it feasible to finish the testing by Friday?
example_zh: 週五前完成測試可行嗎？

zh: 提出（問題）、提醒大家注意
definition: to point out a problem so that other people notice it
example: Thanks for flagging the issue so early.
example_zh: 謝謝你這麼早就提出這個問題。

definition: the range of work that a project includes
example: If we reduce the scope, we can still launch on time.
example_zh: 如果我們縮小範圍，還是可以準時上線。

definition: extra time added to a plan in case something goes wrong
example: Let's add a two-day buffer before the launch.
example_zh: 我們在上線前留兩天緩衝吧。

definition: making progress as planned and likely to succeed on time
example: The mobile app is still on track for a December launch.
example_zh: 行動 App 仍按計畫在十二月上線。

definition: an important stage or event in the progress of a project
example: Finishing the first prototype was a big milestone for the team.
example_zh: 完成第一個原型是團隊的一大里程碑。

definition: a problem that stops work from moving forward until someone solves it
example: The missing API key is our biggest blocker right now.
example_zh: 缺少 API 金鑰是我們目前最大的卡關點。

definition: to make a new product or service available, often in stages
example: We're going to roll out the new design to 10% of users first.
example_zh: 我們會先對 10% 的使用者推出新設計。

definition: to give official approval for something
example: Legal hasn't signed off on the new contract yet.
example_zh: 法務還沒核准新合約。

definition: to contact someone again or take further action about something
example: I'll follow up with the supplier tomorrow morning.
example_zh: 我明天早上會再跟供應商追蹤一下。

definition: (of unfinished work) to be moved to the next period instead of being finished now
example: Two tasks will carry over to next sprint.
example_zh: 有兩項工作會順延到下個 Sprint。

definition: immediately, with only a quick look
example: The dashboard shows the team's progress at a glance.
example_zh: 儀表板讓人一眼就看出團隊進度。

definition: to start to have a minor illness, such as a cold or the flu
example: I always come down with a cold when the weather changes.
example_zh: 每次天氣一變，我就會感冒。

definition: tired and slightly unwell, usually because you have been working too hard
example: After three weeks of late nights, she was feeling completely run-down.
example_zh: 連續熬夜三週後，她覺得整個人都垮了。

definition: if a pain or illness flares up, it suddenly starts again or gets worse
example: My back pain tends to flare up when I sit at my desk for too long.
example_zh: 我在辦公桌前坐太久，背痛就容易發作。

definition: medicine you can buy without a doctor's prescription
example: I've been taking an over-the-counter painkiller, but it only helps for a few hours.
example_zh: 我一直在吃成藥止痛藥，但只撐得了幾個小時。

definition: a written order from a doctor for a specific medicine
example: The doctor gave me a prescription for a stronger cream.
example_zh: 醫生開了比較強效的藥膏處方給我。

definition: an extra, usually unpleasant, effect of a medicine
example: One common side effect of this medicine is feeling sleepy.
example_zh: 這種藥常見的副作用是想睡覺。

definition: the act of sending a patient to a specialist for more tests or treatment
example: If the pain doesn't improve, I'll give you a referral to a specialist.
example_zh: 如果疼痛沒改善，我會幫你轉診給專科醫師。

definition: to rest and avoid working too hard
example: The doctor told me to take it easy for a few days.
example_zh: 醫生叫我這幾天好好休息、別太操。

definition: to start a meeting, project or event
example: We'll kick off the project with a two-hour workshop on Monday.
example_zh: 我們週一會用兩小時的工作坊啟動這個專案。

definition: a specific piece of work that must be finished and handed over as part of a project
example: The main deliverable for this phase is a working prototype.
example_zh: 這個階段主要的交付項目是一個可以運作的原型。

definition: approximate; not exact but close enough to plan with
example: Can you give me a ballpark figure for the budget?
example_zh: 你可以給我一個預算的大概數字嗎？

definition: the person you should go to with questions about a particular area
example: Anna will be our point of contact for anything related to design.
example_zh: 跟設計有關的事，Anna 會是我們的窗口。

definition: a point in a process where work slows down because too much depends on one person or step
example: Legal review has become a bottleneck, so contracts are taking weeks to sign.
example_zh: 法務審查變成了瓶頸，所以合約要好幾週才簽得下來。

zh: 簡短聯絡、確認一下近況
definition: to talk to someone briefly to share updates or check how things are going
example: Let's touch base on Friday to see where we are.
example_zh: 我們週五簡單對一下，看看進度到哪裡。

zh: 取得（大家的）認同與支持
definition: to get people to agree with and support a plan or decision
example: It's hard to get buy-in from other teams if they don't understand why the project matters.
example_zh: 如果其他團隊不懂這個專案為什麼重要，就很難取得他們的支持。

definition: to start something new and make progress immediately, without needing time to get ready
example: The new engineer had read all the docs, so she hit the ground running on day one.
example_zh: 新來的工程師把文件都讀完了，所以第一天就馬上進入狀況。

definition: an estimate of what a number will be in the future, based on current data
example: Our sales projection for next year assumes no new competitors.
example_zh: 我們明年的銷售預測是假設不會有新的競爭對手。

zh: 逐步加大、提高（投入或產量）
definition: to increase the amount or speed of something, usually step by step
example: We're going to ramp up hiring once the new office opens.
example_zh: 新辦公室啟用後，我們會逐步加快招募腳步。

zh: （公司或部門的）人力編制、員額
definition: the number of people employed by a company or team
example: We can't take on the project without more headcount.
example_zh: 沒有增加人力編制，我們接不了這個專案。

definition: to earn exactly as much money as you spend, so there is no profit and no loss
example: The new store should break even in its second year.
example_zh: 新門市應該會在第二年打平。

definition: to look at data or a problem in more detail to find the cause
example: Let's drill down into the numbers by region.
example_zh: 我們按地區深入看一下這些數字。

definition: the most important point that you want people to remember
example: The key takeaway is that customers want faster delivery, not lower prices.
example_zh: 最重要的結論是：顧客要的是更快出貨，而不是更低的價格。

definition: compared with the same period in the previous year
example: Online orders grew 25% year-over-year.
example_zh: 線上訂單比去年同期成長了 25%。

definition: a situation or condition that makes progress more difficult
example: Higher shipping costs were a major headwind this quarter.
example_zh: 運費上漲是這一季主要的不利因素。

definition: a short stop between two flights on the same journey
example: We have a two-hour layover in Bangkok before the flight to Munich.
example_zh: 我們飛慕尼黑之前，要在曼谷轉機停留兩小時。

definition: the second flight you take to continue a journey after changing planes
example: If the first flight is late, I'll miss my connecting flight.
example_zh: 如果第一段班機延誤，我就會錯過轉機航班。

definition: to book a different flight, room, or appointment instead of the original one
example: The agent rebooked me on the first flight the next morning.
example_zh: 櫃檯人員幫我改訂隔天早上的第一班飛機。

definition: waiting to get a seat on a flight that is full, in case someone does not show up
example: The flight is full, so you're on standby for now.
example_zh: 這班飛機客滿了，所以你目前是候補。

definition: a piece of paper or code you can use instead of money for a meal, hotel, or service
example: They gave us a meal voucher for the airport restaurant.
example_zh: 他們給我們一張機場餐廳的餐券。

definition: unable to leave a place, usually because transport is not available
example: Hundreds of passengers were stranded at the airport after the storm.
example_zh: 暴風雨過後，好幾百名旅客滯留在機場。

definition: a small bag you are allowed to take onto the plane with you
example: I always pack a change of clothes in my carry-on.
example_zh: 我總是在隨身行李裡放一套換洗衣物。

definition: money or something else you receive because you have suffered a loss or a problem
example: You may be able to claim compensation for a long delay.
example_zh: 班機延誤很久的話，你也許可以申請賠償。

definition: helpful and intended to improve something
example: Thanks for the constructive comments on my draft.
example_zh: 謝謝你對我的草稿提出有建設性的意見。

definition: to seem to have a particular quality to other people
example: I didn't mean it that way, but my email may have come across as rude.
example_zh: 我不是那個意思，但我的 email 可能給人很沒禮貌的感覺。

definition: something about yourself or a situation that you do not notice
example: Ask a colleague you trust to point out your blind spots.
example_zh: 請一位你信任的同事指出你的盲點。

zh: 把（意見）聽進去並採納（偏英式說法，美國職場也聽得懂）
definition: to listen to advice or criticism and act on it
example: I'll take your comments on board when I revise the plan.
example_zh: 我修改計畫時會把你的意見納入考量。

zh: 偷工減料；省略該做的步驟
definition: to do something quickly or cheaply by skipping important steps
example: We can't cut corners on security testing.
example_zh: 資安測試不能偷工減料。

zh: 挺身而出；承擔更多責任
definition: to take on more responsibility, especially when it is needed
example: When our lead was out sick, Amy stepped up and ran the meeting.
example_zh: 我們的組長請病假時，Amy 挺身而出主持了會議。

definition: when you think about something after it has happened
example: In hindsight, we should have tested the app on older phones.
example_zh: 事後回想，我們應該要在舊手機上測試這個 app。

zh: 遇到某類問題第一個會找的人
definition: the person everyone asks for help with a particular thing
example: Kevin is our go-to person for anything to do with Excel.
example_zh: 跟 Excel 有關的事，大家第一個都找 Kevin。

definition: a period when a system or service is not working
example: The four-hour outage stopped every customer from logging in.
example_zh: 這次四小時的服務中斷讓所有客戶都無法登入。

definition: to pass a problem to someone more senior so they can deal with it
example: If the bug isn't fixed in two hours, escalate it to the engineering lead.
example_zh: 如果兩小時內沒修好這個 bug，就往上呈報給工程主管。

definition: to express strong feelings, especially anger, so that you feel better
example: Let the customer vent for a minute before you explain anything.
example_zh: 在你解釋任何事之前，先讓客戶發洩一下。

definition: a temporary way of getting something done while the real problem is not fixed
example: Until the fix is ready, the workaround is to export the data by hand.
example_zh: 在修好之前，暫時的替代做法是手動匯出資料。

definition: to find out the real cause of a problem
example: Our engineers are working to get to the bottom of the crash.
example_zh: 我們的工程師正在查當機的真正原因。

definition: to be forgotten or not dealt with because nobody is clearly responsible
example: Requests like this can fall through the cracks if nobody owns them.
example_zh: 如果沒人負責，這類請求很容易被忽略。

definition: to allow something that is not usually allowed because of special circumstances
example: We don't usually give refunds, but my manager agreed to bend the rules this time.
example_zh: 我們通常不退款，但這次主管同意通融。

zh: 表達善意的舉動（如補償、優惠）
definition: something you give or do to show that you want to keep a good relationship
example: As a goodwill gesture, we gave the client a month of free service.
example_zh: 為了表達誠意，我們送客戶一個月的免費服務。

definition: a legal agreement to rent a home for a fixed period
example: We signed a one-year lease on Friday.
example_zh: 我們星期五簽了一年的租約。

definition: money you pay a landlord before moving in and get back if nothing is damaged
example: The landlord asked for a security deposit of two months' rent.
example_zh: 房東要收兩個月房租當押金。

definition: basic services such as water, electricity and gas
example: Does the rent include utilities, or do we pay them separately?
example_zh: 房租有包水電瓦斯嗎？還是要另外付？

zh: 讓人直接放棄的關鍵問題
definition: one problem that is serious enough to make you say no
example: No natural light is a deal-breaker for me.
example_zh: 完全沒有自然光，對我來說就是不考慮。

definition: a home in poor condition that needs a lot of repairs
example: It's a fixer-upper, so the price is surprisingly low.
example_zh: 那間需要大整修，所以價格低得驚人。

zh: （入住或退租時）逐間點交檢查
definition: a careful check of a home, room by room, usually with the landlord
example: We did a walk-through and photographed every scratch.
example_zh: 我們逐間檢查了一遍，把每道刮痕都拍下來。

definition: close enough to reach on foot
example: The apartment is within walking distance of a supermarket.
example_zh: 那間公寓走路就能到超市。

definition: to rent out all or part of your rented home to someone else
example: Can I sublet the room while I'm working abroad?
example_zh: 我在國外工作的期間，可以把房間轉租出去嗎？

definition: the act of extending a contract for another period
example: Our contract with the cloud provider is up for renewal in December.
example_zh: 我們和雲端廠商的合約十二月要續約。

definition: a sudden, large increase in price
example: Nobody on the team was happy about the 15% price hike.
example_zh: 團隊裡沒有人對漲價 15% 感到開心。

definition: something that gives you power or an advantage in a negotiation
example: Two cheaper quotes gave us real leverage in the meeting.
example_zh: 兩份比較便宜的報價讓我們在會議上有了真正的籌碼。

definition: money taken off your bill when a supplier fails to keep its promises
example: We received a service credit after the long outage.
example_zh: 那次長時間的服務中斷之後，我們拿到了服務補償金。

definition: to fix a price or deal so that it cannot change later
example: Let's lock in this rate before it goes up again.
example_zh: 趁價格還沒再漲，我們先把這個費率鎖定吧。

definition: to refuse to continue with a deal or negotiation
example: If they won't lower the price, we're ready to walk away.
example_zh: 如果他們不降價，我們準備放棄這筆交易。

definition: to reach a compromise by giving up part of what you want
example: They asked for 10% and we offered 2%, so we agreed to meet them halfway at 6%.
example_zh: 他們要 10%，我們開 2%，所以我們同意各退一步，定在 6%。

definition: to add something extra to make an offer more attractive
example: The vendor offered free training to sweeten the deal.
example_zh: 廠商加碼提供免費訓練，讓條件更吸引人。

definition: to say or do something that helps people relax when they first meet or start talking
example: A quick question about the weekend is an easy way to break the ice.
example_zh: 問一下週末過得如何，是打破冷場的簡單方法。

definition: to start to feel comfortable in a new home, job or place
example: It took me about a month to settle in at the new office.
example_zh: 我花了大約一個月才適應新辦公室。

definition: full of activity, with no time to rest
example: Despite a hectic morning, she joined the call on time.
example_zh: 儘管早上忙得團團轉，她還是準時上線開會。

definition: the trip you make between home and work every day
example: Although my new commute is longer, I can read on the train.
example_zh: 雖然我新的通勤路程比較長，但我可以在火車上看書。

definition: to learn all the latest information you need to do a job
example: Could you help Jun get up to speed before Monday?
example_zh: 你可以在星期一前幫 Jun 掌握最新狀況嗎？

definition: later than planned or expected
example: Sorry, I'm running behind, so please start without me.
example_zh: 抱歉，我晚了一點，請先開始不用等我。

definition: getting better after an illness or injury
example: I had a bad cold last week, but I'm on the mend now.
example_zh: 我上週重感冒，不過現在慢慢好起來了。

definition: a request to be told about any news or changes
example: Good luck with the landlord, and keep me posted on what he says.
example_zh: 祝你跟房東交涉順利，他怎麼回覆隨時告訴我。

definition: a receipt or record that shows you bought something
example: You'll need some proof of purchase, such as a receipt or a bank statement.
example_zh: 你需要提供購買證明，例如收據或銀行對帳單。

definition: money you can only spend in the same shop instead of getting cash back
example: Without a receipt, they could only give me store credit.
example_zh: 因為沒有收據，他們只能給我店內購物金。

definition: not working properly because something is wrong with it
example: If the item is faulty, you can return it even after thirty days.
example_zh: 如果商品有瑕疵，即使超過三十天也可以退。

definition: a fee some stores charge when you return something that isn't broken
example: Opened electronics come with a 10% restocking fee.
example_zh: 已拆封的電子產品要收 10% 的重新上架費。

definition: the box and wrapping that a product came in when you bought it
example: Please bring the lamp back in its original packaging.
example_zh: 請把檯燈連同原包裝一起帶回來。

definition: the number of days after buying something when the shop will still take it back
example: The return window for sale items is only fourteen days.
example_zh: 特價商品的可退貨期限只有十四天。

definition: without asking you to explain why
example: They'll take back any shoes within a month, no questions asked.
example_zh: 一個月內的鞋子他們都收退，不問理由。

definition: to give one thing back and get a different one in its place
example: Could I swap this one for a smaller size?
example_zh: 我可以把這件換成小一號的嗎？

definition: to learn how a job or place works when you are new
example: Priya will help you learn the ropes during your first week.
example_zh: 第一週會由 Priya 帶你熟悉工作的門道。

definition: how quickly or slowly someone can learn a new skill or system
example: Our billing system has a steep learning curve, so don't worry if it feels slow at first.
example_zh: 我們的請款系統很難上手，所以一開始覺得慢也別擔心。

definition: to learn how to do something after some practice
example: It took me a month to get the hang of the reporting tool.
example_zh: 我花了一個月才抓到那個報表工具的訣竅。

definition: to follow an experienced person at work and watch what they do so you can learn
example: On Wednesday, you'll shadow Ken on his client calls.
example_zh: 星期三你會跟著 Ken，在旁邊觀摩他打給客戶的電話。

definition: all the small details of how something works
example: Nobody knows the ins and outs of our expense policy better than Lisa.
example_zh: 沒有人比 Lisa 更清楚我們報帳規定的眉角。

zh: 入職夥伴（帶新人的同事）
definition: a coworker who is chosen to help a new employee with everyday questions
example: If you're not sure who to ask, start with your onboarding buddy. That's the teammate assigned to help you settle in.
example_zh: 如果不確定該問誰，就先問你的入職夥伴，那是公司指派來幫你適應環境的同事。

definition: a diagram that shows who works in which team and who reports to whom
example: I printed the org chart so I could see who reports to whom.
example_zh: 我把組織圖印出來，才看得出誰向誰報告。

definition: special words used by a group of people that others find hard to understand
example: Stop me if I use too much jargon. We have an acronym for everything here.
example_zh: 如果我講太多行話就打斷我。我們這裡什麼都有縮寫。

definition: with your microphone switched off, so other people on the call cannot hear you
example: Sorry, I was on mute. Could you repeat the question?
example_zh: 抱歉，我剛剛是靜音。可以再問一次嗎？

definition: if someone's voice breaks up on a call, you only hear parts of what they say
example: You're breaking up a bit. Can you move closer to your router?
example_zh: 你的聲音有點斷斷續續的，可以靠近路由器一點嗎？

zh: 延遲；畫面或聲音跟不上
definition: a delay between when something happens and when you see or hear it
example: There's a two-second lag, so let's not interrupt each other.
example_zh: 有兩秒的延遲，所以我們不要互相打斷。

definition: to let other people on a video call see what is on your computer screen
example: Let me screen-share the dashboard so we're all looking at the same numbers.
example_zh: 我來分享螢幕給大家看儀表板，這樣大家看的是同一組數字。

definition: to leave a call and join it again, usually to fix a technical problem
example: My video froze, so I'm going to drop off and dial back in.
example_zh: 我的畫面卡住了，我先離開再重新加入。

definition: when two or more people speak at the same time and nobody can be heard clearly
example: We kept talking over each other, so Lena asked everyone to raise a hand first.
example_zh: 我們一直同時講話，所以 Lena 請大家先舉手再發言。

zh: 常出小毛病的；不穩定的
definition: often having small technical problems that stop something from working properly
example: The meeting app has been glitchy all week, so keep the dial-in number handy.
example_zh: 這個會議軟體整個禮拜都不太穩，所以撥入號碼要放在手邊。

definition: to find out why something is not working and try to fix it
example: IT spent an hour trying to troubleshoot my headset before they gave me a new one.
example_zh: IT 花了一個小時想找出我耳機的問題，最後直接給我一副新的。

definition: having accepted more bookings than there are rooms or seats
example: The hotel was overbooked, so two guests had to stay somewhere else.
example_zh: 飯店超額訂房，所以有兩位客人得住到別的地方。

definition: given to customers free of charge
example: Bottled water and coffee are complimentary in every room.
example_zh: 每間客房的瓶裝水和咖啡都是免費招待的。

definition: useful or pleasant facilities at a place, such as a gym, a pool or free Wi-Fi
example: The amenities include a rooftop pool and a 24-hour gym.
example_zh: 飯店設施包括頂樓泳池和 24 小時健身房。

zh: 住宿期間的額外消費（如迷你吧、客房服務）
definition: extra costs during a hotel stay, such as the minibar or room service, on top of the room price
example: A small hold is placed on your card to cover any incidental charges.
example_zh: 飯店會在你的卡上預先保留一小筆金額，用來支付可能的額外消費。

definition: permission to leave your hotel room later than the usual time
example: Could I get a late checkout? My flight isn't until 6 p.m.
example_zh: 可以延後退房嗎？我的班機晚上六點才飛。

zh: 升等（換到更好的房間或座位）
definition: a move to a better room, seat or service, often at no extra cost
example: Because of the mix-up, they gave me a free upgrade to a suite.
example_zh: 因為搞錯了，他們免費幫我升等到套房。

definition: to do something good that reduces the harm of an earlier problem
example: The hotel offered us free breakfast to make up for the long wait.
example_zh: 飯店提供免費早餐，彌補我們等了那麼久。

definition: to deal with a problem or arrangement until it is fixed
example: Give me five minutes and I'll sort out the problem with your booking.
example_zh: 給我五分鐘，我會把你訂房的問題處理好。

definition: the moment when one person or team passes a piece of work to another
example: The handoff between design and engineering went smoothly this time.
example_zh: 這次設計和工程之間的交接很順利。

definition: a person or group who is affected by a project and cares about its result
example: We need to update every stakeholder before we change the launch date.
example_zh: 改上線日期之前，我們要先通知每一位相關人員。

definition: how long it takes to finish a request after you receive it
example: Their usual turnaround time for a data request is three working days.
example_zh: 他們處理一份資料需求通常要三個工作天。

zh: 把（某人）拉進來一起討論
definition: to include someone in a conversation or email so they know what is happening
example: Let me loop in Priya, since she owns the customer database.
example_zh: 我把 Priya 拉進來，因為客戶資料庫是她負責的。

zh: 各自為政、不互通的部門
definition: a team or department that works on its own and rarely shares information with other teams
example: When every department works in a silo, simple questions take weeks to answer.
example_zh: 每個部門都各做各的時候，簡單的問題也要好幾週才有答案。

definition: a short warning that tells someone about something before it happens
example: Thanks for the heads-up about the system maintenance on Friday.
example_zh: 謝謝你先提醒我們週五系統要維修。

zh: 負責到底的態度；主導權
definition: the responsibility for a task, so that you make sure it gets done
example: Mei took ownership of the report and fixed the numbers herself.
example_zh: Mei 把這份報告扛下來，自己把數字修好了。

definition: a list of work that is waiting to be done because there hasn't been time for it yet
example: The data team has a backlog of forty requests, so ours will have to wait.
example_zh: 資料團隊累積了四十個待處理的需求，所以我們的要排隊。

definition: earlier than the planned time
example: The design work is a week ahead of schedule, so we can start testing early.
example_zh: 設計工作超前一週，所以我們可以提早開始測試。

definition: to finish the last part of a task or meeting
example: Let's wrap up the testing by Friday and launch next week.
example_zh: 我們星期五前把測試收尾，下週上線吧。

definition: stopped for now, waiting to continue later
example: The budget request is on hold until finance replies.
example_zh: 預算申請先擱置，等財務部回覆。

zh: 待辦事項（有指定負責人）
definition: a specific task that someone agrees to do after a meeting
example: I've added the server check as an action item for the IT team.
example_zh: 我把伺服器檢查列為 IT 團隊的待辦事項了。

definition: being planned or prepared, and coming soon
example: A second training session is in the pipeline for early December.
example_zh: 第二場訓練課程正在籌備中，預計十二月初。

definition: (of a date or plan) to move later than planned
example: The offsite has slipped by one week because the hotel was full.
example_zh: 因為飯店客滿，員工旅遊往後延了一週。

definition: a short summary of the main points
example: Here's a quick recap of what happened this week.
example_zh: 以下是這週發生的事情的簡短回顧。

definition: waiting to be decided or dealt with
example: Two decisions are still pending, so I'll update you next week.
example_zh: 還有兩件事尚未決定，我下週再跟大家更新。
